clue.text: Monopolise the laundry? Rubbish!

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to oneself
the wash is the batch of clothes being laundered

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of taking over the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is nonsense, an exclamation dismissing something as worthless talk.

clue.text: Old soldier fired in anticipation

indicators.note: in places the word for fired inside the word for anticipation

parts.note: hope is anticipation of something good
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A veteran shot eagerly ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was a heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Recover personal property and exact vengeance

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves their belongings and takes revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally reclaiming what belongs to you; idiomatically, to take revenge on someone who wronged you.

clue.text: Spots a knight in Anglican church

indicators.note: in places the knight's letter inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight with a rash is seen in a Church of England building.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, which are spots.

clue.text: Laughing when the siren sounds

explanation.surface: Someone laughs as an alarm goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooting is loud laughter, and it is also the noise of a horn or siren blaring.

clue.text: Hard hit despite hard work

explanation.surface: A batsman strikes the ball hard even though the going is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A slog is a wild, powerful swipe at a ball, and also a long, tiring grind of effort.

clue.text: Resolve the issue, or get reprimand

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fix the problem or face a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort out a problem is to settle it; to sort someone out is to deal firmly with them, a rebuke.

clue.text: An expression of pain from Oxford University church

parts.note: OU can stand for Oxford University

explanation.surface: A cry of distress comes from a college chapel at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation people make when hurt.

clue.text: Where cinema-fans may jump up in an attack of hysteria!

definitions.text: Where cinema-fans may jump up in an attack of hysteria!

parts.words: Where cinema-fans may jump up in an attack of hysteria
parts.note: jumping insects in a scruffy picture house make the audience leap up, and an attack of hysteria is a fit

explanation.surface: Moviegoers leap from their seats in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLEAPIT is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema; fleas jump, and a fit is an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedy old cinema is jokingly imagined as infested with jumping insects.

clue.text: Napoleon had next to nothing of a body

parts.note: little means very small, next to nothing
corporal means relating to the body

explanation.surface: The French emperor had almost nothing of a physique.
explanation.walkthrough: The Little Corporal was the affectionate nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's soldiers nicknamed him for his early rank and modest height.

clue.text: Applied to be employed with a firm of solicitors

definitions.text: to be employed with a firm of solicitors

explanation.surface: Someone describes joining a law firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory put into practice is applied in reality; read literally, a lawyer put into a practice joins a legal firm.

clue.text: No one returns to a Scottish island

indicators.note: returns signals that the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Nobody goes back to a remote Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: He leads one into conspiracy

indicators.note: into tells us the word for one is placed inside the word for conspiracy

parts.note: a plot is a secret scheme
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A ringleader draws someone into a secret plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides or steers, for example a ship into harbour, so is someone who leads the way.

clue.text: Advance by backing favourites

indicators.note: backing tells us the word for favourites is turned round, read from the back

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A punter gets ahead by betting on the favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: To step forward is to move ahead, so advance and step are synonyms.

clue.text: Strain is mounting by the end of the day

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting reads the word is upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
eve is evening, the close of the day

explanation.surface: Tension builds as evening falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain liquid is to pass it through a mesh, as a sieve does.

clue.text: The best man serves him curry

explanation.surface: At a wedding, the best man brings him a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is attended by his best man; to curry a horse is to brush it, a sense of groom.

clue.text: Following points put against taking legal action

indicators.note: put against signals one piece placed directly beside the next

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
suing is taking someone to court

explanation.surface: Someone describes arguments raised against going to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing describes what comes next or results, a synonym of subsequent.

clue.text: People involved in breach of duty cause anguish

indicators.note: involved in places the word for people inside the word for a breach of duty

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law, a breach of a duty owed
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk caught up in a legal wrong suffer distress.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong such as negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment is to inflict suffering, making someone feel great distress.

clue.text: We appear in US helicopter at all events

indicators.note: in places the word we inside the word for the helicopter action

parts.note: in American usage, to helicopter (as a helicopter parent does) is to hover
taken as written

explanation.surface: We feature aboard an American chopper in any case.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'helicopter' as the American verb for hovering over someone, as an anxious parent does.
explanation.definitionFit: However can mean nevertheless or in any case, the same sense as at all events.

clue.text: She was depicted by him with features drawn

explanation.surface: A woman's portrait was sketched by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, so 'him' is its author.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard wrote the novel She; a gaunt face with drawn features looks haggard.

clue.text: Fascinated by bestial doctor in dire distress

indicators.note: in puts the doctor inside the rearranged letters
distress signals the letters of dire are jumbled

parts.note: a vet is a doctor for animals

explanation.surface: Someone was gripped by the plight of an animal doctor in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bestial' looks like an insult but simply marks an animal doctor; 'distress' and 'in' are both signals, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveted describes attention held completely, as if fixed in place.

clue.text: Decline to let one's passengers leave

explanation.surface: A driver describes letting riders out of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-off is a fall or decrease, and to drop people off is to let them out of a vehicle.

clue.text: Numerous streams of traffic may delay them

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
rivers are streams

explanation.surface: Heavy streams of traffic hold up motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists are slowed by congestion on the roads.

clue.text: Condition upsetting to senior sportsman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: if introduces a condition
an elder is someone older, a senior

explanation.surface: A medical condition upsets an older athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder is a player in cricket or baseball who retrieves the ball.

clue.text: I beg to be dissociated from derisive comment

indicators.note: dissociated letters are broken apart and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to be kept apart from a mocking remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a taunt or jeer, a remark made to mock.

clue.text: Article invalid has to steer clear of

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
void means of no legal force, invalid

explanation.surface: An invalid document must be shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from it, a synonym of shun.

clue.text: English sports require energy, especially for a swordsman

parts.note: PE, physical education, covers school sports
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: English fencing needs vigour, above all from the fencer.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a fencing sword, a weapon made for a fencer.

clue.text: Regret involving head of state in deception

indicators.note: involving means the word for regret wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Remorse about a leader caught in a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem meant to mislead.

clue.text: He never had a mother

annotationWithheld.why: 'He never had a mother' (4): ADAM is hidden in 'had a mother' as an &lit, but no clue word signals the hidden word, and a cryptic-definition reading is refused because its words spell the answer

clue.text: Bill needs payment when the tale has been told

definitions.text: when the tale has been told

explanation.surface: An invoice falls due once a story is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An account rendered is an invoice already sent and awaiting settlement; literally it is a story that has been delivered.

clue.text: Nurse takes time to reach a conclusion

parts.note: the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: A nurse takes a while to get to a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to look after them, which is to tend them.

clue.text: One who gets a taste for embroidery work

explanation.surface: Someone who tries a little of something is drawn to needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster tries small amounts of things; a sampler is also a cloth panel stitched to show off needlework skills.
